name: Audio Leveling And Track Hygiene
use_when: Dialogue, music, and SFX need to be balanced in a YouTube edit.
The timeline has quiet words, loud SFX, or red/clipped levels.
The agent needs a clean track structure before export.
A Resolve Fairlight mix needs clip, track, bus, EQ, dynamics, and routing checks.
A CapCut project needs music to rise under B-roll or product clips and duck under speech using volume keyframes.
avoid_when: The user only requested a silent visual edit.
Audio levels are already mixed and locked by a dedicated sound pass.
Creative distortion or clipping is intentional and approved.

timeline_pattern.pattern: separate_dialogue_music_sfx_ambience -> normalize_or_gain_stage -> keyframe_or_range_repair -> bus_related_tracks -> duck_music -> fade_edges -> loudness_qc
timeline_pattern.track_rule: Keep dialogue, music, SFX, and ambience on separate tracks or logical groups.
timeline_pattern.keyframe_rule: Use volume keyframes for quiet or loud words instead of changing the entire clip when only one moment needs repair.
timeline_pattern.music_duck_rule: Use paired music keyframes before and after speech so the first word is already clear and music restores only after the phrase ends.
timeline_pattern.peak_rule: Avoid red/clipped peaks; leave headroom before export.
timeline_pattern.fairlight_rule: In Fairlight, use clip edits, track faders, and buses deliberately; make sure buses route to the main output.

motion.rule: No direct motion rule; avoid adding visual effects while an audio repair is being judged.

sound.rule: Speech is the anchor. Music and SFX support it unless the section is intentionally music-led.

keyframe_values.dialogue_ceiling: Keep dialogue and full mix out of red; use a practical ceiling around -3 dBFS before platform loudness checks.
keyframe_values.music_duck: Duck music before important words begin, then restore after the phrase or beat.
keyframe_values.capcut_music_duck: In CapCut, very low music values such as 1-2 can be a starting point under speech, but final level must be judged by ear and phone preview.
keyframe_values.fade_edges: Use short fades on SFX/music clips to avoid clicks and abrupt exits.
keyframe_values.mono_rule: Use mono for centered simple sounds when stereo movement is not part of the design.
keyframe_values.fairlight_bus_rule: Route grouped SFX or dialogue to a bus when shared EQ, reverb, compression, or volume control is needed.
keyframe_values.dialogue_compression: Use only modest gain reduction on dialogue, then makeup gain; stop before compression sounds crushed.

captions.rule: Captions support intelligibility but do not excuse buried dialogue.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use loudnorm, volume, afade, acrossfade, pan for mono/stereo decisions, and astats/ebur128 checks. Render waveform review clips around repaired words.
implementation.remotion: Represent dialogue, music, and SFX as separate audio components with gain envelopes and ducking intervals.
implementation.blender: Use the VSE waveform and keyframed volume for animated inserts with narration.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Put music and SFX on separate tracks, use Normalize when useful, place manual volume keyframes before speech, lower music under dialogue, restore after speech clears, and use fade handles for edges.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use track organization, Essential Sound, Submixes, clip gain, manual volume keyframes, fades, EQ/dynamics, and loudness/waveform review.

common_mistakes: Letting SFX or music hit red because the timeline feels more exciting.
Raising a whole clip when only one quiet word needs a keyframe.
Mixing all audio on one track and losing control late in the edit.
Using captions instead of fixing a buried line.
Starting the music duck after speech begins.
Restoring music under the tail of a sentence.
Routing tracks to a bus that is not feeding the main output.
Overcompressing dialogue until noise and breaths become distracting.
qc: Do dialogue, music, and SFX live on controllable tracks or layers?
Does any audible peak clip or hit red?
Are quiet story-critical words repaired with gain or keyframes?
Does music duck before important dialogue, not after it is masked?
Does music restore only after the dialogue phrase clears?
Do SFX fades prevent clicks and harsh edges?
Do all buses route audibly to the main output?
Does dialogue compression improve clarity without sounding crushed?
